label: Michael Shellenberger
narrative: Shellenberger is the person who put a purported unacknowledged special access program into the Congressional Record. On the morning of 13 November 2024 he delivered to Congress a twelve-page document describing Immaculate Constellation as a central or parent USAP consolidating UAP observations from tasked and untasked collection platforms and holding high-quality imagery and measurement-and-signature intelligence; Chairwoman Nancy Mace moved it into the Record from the dais during the hearing, where it appears in the Index of Documents as 'Report, Pentagon, Immaculate Constellation; submitted by Rep. Mace.' Under adversarial questioning from Rep. Clay Higgins he confirmed he knows the author and the sources, has confidence in them, and was withholding their identity by choice. The Pentagon, through spokesperson Sue Gough, says it has no record of such a programme; former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick denied its existence. Neither AARO annual report since - FY2024 or FY2025 - addresses it, and Kosloski's Senate statement for the record does not mention it. In 2025 a separate self-identified whistleblower claimed to have found the programme inside a folder labelled '2018 Schriever Wargame'; analyst Jason Colavito argued that person had mistaken fictitious wargame scenario documents for a real programme. That claim goes to the 2025 claimant's provenance story, not automatically to the 2024 twelve-page report, and the distinction is one the board keeps open rather than collapsing in either direction.
